title: Field Guide
subtitle: Moxie's notebook. If it's written here, I watched it happen twice.
lockedText: Blank page. Haven't met it yet.

baseline.note: Hit numbers are for the starting loadout (Splice Blade: light 1.0, heavy 1.8). Other blades shift them; the rules do not move.
baseline.counting: Beats are counted 1-2-3-4 inside a bar. Count 1 is the first beat of the room.
baseline.placements: A room can re-time or re-armour a machine. The deck readout wins over this page.

groups.title: Machines
groups.blurb: They follow rules. Rules can be led around by the nose.

groups.title: Traps
groups.blurb: Don't care who I am. Don't care who anyone is. Useful.

groups.title: Tape
groups.blurb: What the deck keeps, and what it doesn't.

groups.title: Force
groups.blurb: Hitting things. How hard, and where they end up.

groups.title: Gear
groups.blurb: What I'm wearing. All four of me.

entries.title: Grunt
entries.rule: Walks at the nearest living self. Strikes on every second beat.
notes: It only winds up if someone is inside its reach half a beat before its beat. Not there then? It skips the swing and waits two more beats.
It picks again on every beat, so a closer self takes it off a farther one right on the count. Dead-level tie goes to the earlier tape.
Aim locks when the wind-up starts. Step out of the 120-degree swing, or roll, and it hits air.

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: winds up at 0.9 tiles, hits out to 1.2

entries.title: Stalker
entries.rule: Hunts the farthest living self. Chooses on the bar line, then commits. Strikes on the off beats.
notes: Park a self at the far end of the room and it crosses the whole floor to get there. Everything on the way is where I want it to walk.
Once its prey is within 2.5 tiles it stops reconsidering. It only picks again after it lunges, or if the prey dies or skips.
Faster than a half-speed me. A 0.5x tape cannot outrun it; a 1x tape can.

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: winds up at 0.9 tiles, hits out to 1.2, 90-degree lunge

entries.title: Turret
entries.rule: Bolted down. Shoots the nearest living self it can see, on every second beat.
notes: It chooses a full beat before it fires and tracks until the shot. Nobody in sight at that moment means no shot for two beats.
Walls and shut doors stop its bolts. Low barriers do not. Its bolts hit other machines too: one damage and a flinch.
It never looks at a dead or skipping self. Those cross the lane for free.

entries.title: Shielder
entries.rule: The first hit only pops the shield. A hit from a different self within one beat lands, and the shield snaps back.
notes: One of me can never hurt it, at any speed. My own second hit is just another pop.
Two hit points. The follow-up has to carry 2 to finish it in one go: a 2x light, or a 1x heavy on the run. Otherwise pop it twice.
Traps and other machines' bolts clang off without popping anything. It has to be two of me.

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: winds up at 0.9 tiles, hits out to 1.2

entries.title: Brute
entries.rule: Walks at the nearest living self. Slams once a bar. Small hits hurt it but never move it.
notes: A hit under momentum 3 chips it and nothing else. At 3 or more it gets shoved and staggered, and a stagger cancels the slam.
The slam covers 240 degrees. The only safe ground near it is square behind, or out past 1.7 tiles.
It stands still for a full beat after the slam. It is also heavy enough to hold a heavy plate down for me.

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: winds up at 1.4 tiles, hits out to 1.7

numbers.label: One-hit kill
numbers.value: 2x light on the run, or 2x heavy

entries.title: Drone
entries.rule: Hovers five tiles from the nearest living self. Fires on the off-beat, never on the beat.
notes: Its aim locks half a beat before the shot. Move sideways after the lock and the bolt goes where I was.
Every self closer than five tiles pushes it away, and the pushes add up. Two of me can pin it between us.
Flies over low barriers and pits. Walls and shut doors stop it. It never weighs down a plate, and spikes cannot reach it.

entries.title: The Archivist
entries.rule: Watches the nearest self. Only a self it is not watching can hurt it, and only from behind. It has read every take I committed.
notes: It strikes the spots a committed take stood still for two beats, and the spots it attacked from. While it does, it is watching that old take, so everyone else gets its back.
A take I threw away never reached it. Only commits and a full wipe change what it knows.
It cannot be shoved. A hit of momentum 4 through the back staggers it and cancels whatever it was winding up, memory strikes included.

numbers.label: Attacks on
numbers.value: count 1 of every bar; twice a bar in its last third

numbers.label: Cleave
numbers.value: 150 degrees, catches me within 3.4 tiles of its centre

numbers.label: Below 2/3 health
numbers.value: every other attack is a ring, 6 tiles; walls stop it, a roll passes it

numbers.label: Memory strike
numbers.value: about 1.5 tiles round the remembered spot, 2-beat warning, walls do not shelter

entries.title: Spikes
entries.rule: Floor that kills while it is raised, and only while it is raised.
notes: A roll carries me across raised spikes. A recorded roll does the same on playback.
Machines on the floor take 1 on contact and 1 more for each full beat they stay. Grunts and stalkers die on contact.
Drones float over. Shielders and the Archivist ignore the damage: a trap is not one of me.

numbers.label: Blocks
numbers.value: nothing: not movement, shots or sight

entries.title: Crusher
entries.rule: Kills on the stroke. After that it is just a wall until it pulls back.
notes: Out, it blocks everything a shut door blocks: bodies, shots, flame, sight. A moving shield, if I time it.
A take whose path runs through an extended piston skips there, and its spark waits for the piston to retract.
The stroke deals 3 to any machine under it, drones included. That is a brute in one.

numbers.label: Stroke damage
numbers.value: 3 to machines; a self dies unless rolling

entries.title: Conveyor
entries.rule: Carries whatever stands on it. Never carries a recorded self.
notes: The ride is baked into the take. Reverse the belt later and that take still glides the old way.
It moves machines while they walk, fight, stagger or sleep. It will deliver a sleeping grunt into a swing I recorded earlier.
It runs in world time. On a 2x take it feels half as fast under my feet.

numbers.label: Speed
numbers.value: 2 tiles/s unless the room says otherwise

numbers.label: Carries
numbers.value: walking machines, the live self, low shots

entries.title: Flame Jet
entries.rule: Burns every tile in its lane while it is on. Stops at the first thing that stops a shot.
notes: A shut door, an unbroken wall or an extended crusher cuts the jet short. Open the door and the fire is through that instant.
Low barriers do not stop it, and bodies do not shade what is behind them.
It burns drones too. Prism Goggles do nothing here; they are for lasers.

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: set by the room, in whole tiles

entries.title: Dart Launcher
entries.rule: Fires straight down its lane on its beat. Aims at nothing. Cannot be broken.
notes: A dart stops in the first living thing it touches, me or a machine. A machine in the lane is cover.
It deals 1 and a flinch to a machine. Knock something into the lane just before the beat.
It flies over low barriers. Walls, shut doors, unbroken walls and extended crushers stop it.

numbers.label: Fires
numbers.value: every 2 beats unless the room says otherwise

entries.title: Bumper
entries.rule: Fires once each time its signal comes on. Throws whatever stands on it. Never throws a recorded self.
notes: It is a free knockback: no damage, but it breaks a wind-up, and a machine thrown into a wall staggers.
Heavier machines fly shorter: a brute goes a third of the distance.
It throws the live me the full distance, and the flight is recorded as plain movement. A door shut across that flight later makes the take skip.

numbers.label: Re-arms
numbers.value: when its signal goes off and on again

entries.title: Beam Sensor
entries.rule: A tripwire. On while a living body is in the beam. Hurts nothing.
notes: Machines trip it too, awake or asleep. A grunt walked through the beam opens the door for me.
Dead takes, skipping takes, sparks and shots do not trip it. A take that dies before the beam leaves the door shut.
The beam ends at the first wall, shut door or extended crusher. Anything past that is not seen.

numbers.label: Sees
numbers.value: selves, machines or both, set by the room

entries.title: Relay
entries.rule: Takes a trigger and answers on the beat: a pulse, a latch or a toggle.
notes: It does one job at a time. Triggers that arrive while it is armed or pulsing are ignored.
Its lamp is lit from trigger to firing. That lamp is my warning for whatever it drives.
It turns 'something walked through' into 'the crusher slams on the next beat'. I can count that.

numbers.label: Fires on
numbers.value: the next whole beat, unless the room says otherwise

numbers.label: Pulse length
numbers.value: 1 beat unless the room says otherwise

entries.title: Magnet
entries.rule: Drags every machine in range toward it. Never drags me.
notes: Walls do not shield from the pull. Machines keep thinking and swinging while they slide.
Lighter means faster: drones come quickest, a brute at a third of a grunt's pace. Turrets do not budge.
It gathers a spread-out crowd into one swing's arc, or holds a drone where a flame lane runs.

entries.title: Laser
entries.rule: Kills a living, in-sync self that touches the beam while it is on. Machines walk through it.
notes: A roll crosses it. So does a dead take, and so does a skipping one.
It is on exactly while its signal is on. Find the plate or switch and the beam is somebody's job.
Prism Goggles make every one of me immune. Nothing else in the room respects them.

entries.title: Tape Speed
entries.rule: Every take records for the same length of time. A fast tape lives in a slow world and plays back short; a slow tape plays back long.
notes: At 2x, machines move at half pace while I record, and my take fills half as many bars on playback.
Swings carry the tape's speed: a 2x light hits like two. A 0.5x light will not drop a grunt.
Machines keep their own beat whatever speed I pick. Speed changes how many of their beats my take covers.

numbers.label: Speeds
numbers.value: 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x (the room chooses which are on offer)

entries.title: The Count-In
entries.rule: Four beats, five-six-seven-eight, then the room starts from its first beat. Every take starts on that same beat.
notes: The room is identical at the top of every take. What a machine does on beat nine, it does on beat nine again, unless one of me changed something.
The count is at the base tempo whatever the tape speed.
No pausing to think once it starts. A pause during the count or the take throws the take away.

entries.title: Retry, Commit, Reset
entries.rule: Retry throws away the take I just made. Commit locks it and arms the next cassette. Reset wipes all four.
notes: Nothing is kept unless I say so. A committed tape can only be changed by wiping every tape.
The room does not need all four. The first combined run that wins, wins.
A win needs the job done and at least one of me alive when the tape runs out.

numbers.label: Cassettes
numbers.value: up to 4, fewer in some rooms

entries.title: Dying on Tape
entries.rule: One hit kills. The take keeps rolling: I finish it as a ghost that walls still stop and nothing can hurt.
notes: What the ghost does counts in that take only. On playback a dead take walks its path through everything and touches nothing.
So a door only my ghost opened stays shut next run, unless a later take keeps that self alive.
Machines never aim at a dead take. It is no good as bait.

numbers.label: Roll
numbers.value: 2.4 tiles, untouchable for most of it

entries.title: Rescue
entries.rule: Who lives is worked out fresh every run. Stop the thing that killed an earlier take and everything it recorded after that becomes real.
notes: It cuts both ways: a take that used to survive can die sooner once the room has changed, and its later actions stop counting.
Recording past my own death is laying down a route for a self I plan to save.
A rescued take can still skip if its old route is blocked now. Alive is not the same as on time.

entries.title: Skipping and the Spark
entries.rule: If a take's next step is blocked, the picture carries on and the girl is left behind as a spark that has to run round and catch up.
notes: A skipping take does nothing and nothing can hurt it. Machines stop aiming at it. It crosses a firing lane for free.
The spark cannot open, press or hit anything, and it never gives up or jumps. If the way round is sealed, it waits.
A skipping take that is alive at the end still counts as a survivor. It cannot hold the exit.

numbers.label: Rejoins
numbers.value: within 0.35 tiles of the picture, with a clear line

numbers.label: Blocked by
numbers.value: walls, shut doors, unbroken walls, low barriers, extended crushers

entries.title: Stop, Repeat, Reverse
entries.rule: When a tape runs out it stops and holds, cuts back to its start, or plays backward. Every action fires again each pass.
notes: A stopped take is still a body: it holds a plate, draws aim and can be killed where it stands.
On a backward pass a switch flips back and a swing swings again. But a run-up is now a retreat, so that swing lands at 3/4 of a standing hit instead of 1 1/2.
Dead stays dead across the loop. On a repeat the picture jumps to the start; a spark has to travel there.

numbers.label: Stop
numbers.value: holds the last pose to the end of the room's time

numbers.label: Repeat
numbers.value: a 4x take loops four times for each pass of a 1x take

entries.title: Momentum
entries.rule: Momentum is the swing's weight times the tape's speed, plus up to half again for running into it. Whole points of momentum are damage.
notes: Running straight in adds 50%. Backing away takes 25% off. Standing still is the plain number.
Tape speed counts once. A 2x standing light is 2; a 2x heavy on the run is 5.4.
Shots do not carry tape speed. Once it leaves the weapon it belongs to the room.

entries.title: Knockback
entries.rule: A hit that does not kill shoves the machine: momentum divided by its weight, in tiles, three at most. It carries on from where it lands.
notes: A shove breaks a wind-up. The machine then waits for its next beat; it never swings off the beat.
Shoved into a wall, the leftover distance turns into stagger.
Machines never shove a recorded self. They kill it or they do nothing.

numbers.label: Wall slam
numbers.value: 1/4 second of stagger per tile left over

entries.title: Stagger
entries.rule: A hit that does not kill freezes the machine: momentum divided by its poise, in seconds. A stagger cancels a wind-up.
notes: A staggered machine does not walk, pick a target or wind up. Whoever it was chasing gets that time.
A brute only staggers from momentum 3 or more, the Archivist from 4 through its back. With the Splice Blade, a hit that big kills a fresh brute anyway.
Trap hits and stray bolts give a flat quarter second instead.

numbers.label: Poise
numbers.value: stalker 1.5, drone 1.5, grunt 2, shielder 2.5, brute 6, Archivist 20

entries.title: Breakable Walls
entries.rule: One swing with enough momentum breaks it. Weak swings clang and do not add up.
notes: Until it breaks it is a wall: it stops shots, flame and darts, and a take whose path runs through it skips.
Only a swing breaks it. Shots do not.
Each wall has its own number, and a clang shows what was missing. Speed and a run-up are the cheap ways to find it.

numbers.label: Standard wall
numbers.value: 5: a 2x heavy on the run, or a 4x heavy

numbers.label: Not enough
numbers.value: 2x standing heavy (3.6), 1x heavy on the run (2.7)

entries.title: Six Slots
entries.rule: Helmet, top, pants, shoes, melee, ranged. One loadout, worn by all four takes, locked while I am in the room.
notes: Gear changes between rooms only, so a committed tape never means something different later.
A find is mine for good once I clear its room. Swapping costs nothing.
Every room on the way down can be done in what I walked in wearing.

numbers.label: Starting kit
numbers.value: Scrap Cap, Lined Bomber, Olive Cargos, Beater High-Tops, Splice Blade, Mixtape Rocket

entries.title: Shots
entries.rule: The tape keeps when, where and which way I fired. Everything after the trigger is the room's business.
notes: The same recorded shot can hit, miss or find a different machine next run. The take did not change; the room did.
Only a living, in-sync self fires. A shot already in the air keeps flying if she dies.
Recharge runs on the tape's own clock, so a 2x take recharges in half the world's time.

numbers.label: Shot momentum
numbers.value: the weapon's own; tape speed not added

entries.title: Homing Rocket
entries.rule: Locks the nearest living machine once, at launch. Chases only that one. Very slow.
notes: Nearest is measured at launch on each run. Shove a different machine closer before the trigger and the same old shot picks the new one.
It needs no line of sight to lock, but walls still stop it. If its target dies it flies straight on.
It hits whatever machine it touches first, locked or not.

entries.title: Piercing Shot
entries.rule: Fast and straight. Passes through machines, hitting each once, and stops in the last one it is allowed.
notes: The puzzle is the line. Knockback and bait are how I draw it.
Walls and shut doors stop it like any shot.

entries.title: Wall-Passer
entries.rule: Goes through walls, shut doors and unbroken walls. Stops in the first machine it touches.
notes: Slow and short. The machine has to be where the shot will be, not where it was.
It ends at the edge of the map and nowhere before that but a machine.

entries.title: Lobbed Shell
entries.rule: Flies over everything and bursts where it lands, a fixed distance out. Nothing in between is touched.
notes: It cannot land close. Anything nearer than the landing spot is safe from it.
Walls shield machines from the burst, unless the shell lands on top of the wall.
The burst pushes machines away from its centre.

numbers.label: Flight
numbers.value: 7 tiles/s, so one second in the air

entries.title: Short Burst
entries.rule: A fan of pellets, each a full hit, each stopping in the first thing it touches. Gone after a few tiles.
notes: Point-blank, several pellets land on one machine and the damage stacks.
Quickest recharge there is, which matters most on a fast tape.
